title: The copy grader's score didn't predict replies: don't rewrite to please it
hypothesis: Copy that scores higher on gtme-grade gets more replies.
change: Compared the grader's score with measured reply rates for the founder-story opener.

oracle.baseline: Jonah-list campaigns, 35 replies from 474 people, about two emails each

result: The founder-story opener scored 30 to 45 of 100 (85 ships), yet got 22 replies from 331 people (6.6%) with one email each, against 7.4% for the comparison. Too close to call, different lists and weeks. On 10-12 a rewrite chasing the rubric to 90 produced contrived lines Sagar wouldn't send.
next_decision: Split test the founder-story opener against a recipient-first opener at equal volume before trusting either the grader or a hunch.
check: Never change copy only to raise a grade. A copy change needs a split test sized to detect the lift (about 1,300 people per arm for 6.6% to 9.6%). `gtme-learning split` also refuses an arm under the powered size for the observed gap.
scope: Founder-led cold email. The grader may still catch compliance and rendering faults; this is about its copy rubric.
